items.note: S2.1.1 states the eight-row gadget on triples of [100] giving y_S+x_S for arbitrary scratch, and S2.1.2 reproduces the three-stage composition (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) of lines 761-763. The gadget's own proof (net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch, central coefficients |S∩T| mod 2 or (|S∩T|-1)/2 cancelled by the side wires, lines 741-759) is only quoted, not shown.

S2.2 gives common frames, the edge change D_vD_u^{-1}, commutation with pointwise gates and the route operator D_sink D_source^{-1}. It leaves out the route sign ε_w (lines 818-822), which the complex network needs.

S2.3 has nested nondegenerate labels built from tensor products of triple lines in an m-dimensional space, with comparable labels on every edge. It omits the only decreasing edges (central 3->4, losing h), L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L and L/N<1/2. It also calls the label sum 's', which for the bit network is s_b minus N.

S2.4 states the endpoint identity M_sink(ρ(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, the shear H<-H+D on every role and s_b<W_b m. It does not say the matrices are projections P_U with source -P_{U_a}, and it omits s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

S2.5 states one translation kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector and s_c<W_c m. It says telescoping gives C^{⊗m} but omits the source and sink diagonal corrections (Z_a, i^27) and the undoing of the signed exchange that the paper needs (lines 1225-1227, 1297-1314). It also omits the definition of C_U and the formula s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c.

The plan states s_b<W_b m, s_c<W_c m, τ=1-2^{-50} and s_b/W_b<m^τ. It never gives L<N/2, the deficits η_b and η_c, or the argument η>20·2^{-50} with log m<20. The source of the strict inequality is asserted, not shown.
S1.2 and S1.3 restate both lemmas faithfully, and the quoted line carries the b^{O(1)} offset condition. No proof is given.

The statements are correct, and the method follows the paper: top-row pivot elimination, then triangular conjugation by controlled shifts. It omits the key step that each one of Π, H_i<-H_i+D_j, is done as D_j<-D_j+H_i, a swap, D_j<-H_i-D_j, using exactly one interchange (lines 1436-1443). It also omits the choice of the prime q.

These steps follow the paper's proof: cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Φ_{A_e} on each edge, H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three-shear interchange, s calls giving F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule at O(V) per node.

The O(Vu^τ) bound, row padding and the base-m split are stated. It omits that the row field is made from the chunks' own top ρ=O(log e) digits and that binary ranges are padded to [q^e]. 'Arbitrary row counts' hides where the rows come from.

S4.2 matches lines 1903-1916: s_c child calls on f=e/m axes plus a fixed number of binary row additions. S4.3 gives H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D, and S4.1 gives the kernel identities. The P_M conjugation and the inverse-child identity are not given.
S4.4 gives the positions ρ+iK, the restored third chunk, eight cyclic shifts, repair of a bad set of density 80(f-1)2^{-K}, and the cost O(V(L^τ+1)) in its parameter-family form.

The row split to V/W streams and F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^τ+1) are correct. The leaves F(e)=O(e) for e<d^β, the base-m pieces and the condition on λ' are missing. S4.6 uses a<m^λ where the paper needs a<=m^σ.

The sub-steps follow the proof at 2686-2758: the phase reduction to s_c children, the row split, packed row additions, the recurrence, conversion of C-layers to H_0 layers, Δ=⌈C_0d^{C_1}⌉=o(p) guard bits with p+Δ and Δ+3 bits, and one truncation with error below √2·2^{-p}. The arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E behind Δ is not shown.

Contraction, character cancellation (proved directly because the ring has zero divisors), decimation in frequency and bit-reversed storage follow the paper. The layout L and the cost bound O(Tp[dK+pK^{τ-1}+ℓd^{λ'}]) are only quoted in T2.3, with no derivation.
T2.4 gives evaluation at 2^{4p}, the established multiplier, centered coefficient extraction and the O(rp log(rp)) cost.

T2.5 gives the procedure: two forward transforms in LB order, pointwise products divided by r, the opposite transform and scaling by M. It gives the error √2·M(3ℓ+1)2^{-p} but omits the proposition's cost bound.

These steps follow the paper's route: the identity TP_sF_s=P_tF_tS, N=CTD with ||N-I||<2^{-α^2θ}, Neumann inversion, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C, the one-dimensional approximations, then tensoring with error, time and axis-movement costs.
Both the permuted chirp identity and the source-permutation cancellation are stated as in the lemma.

The sizes b, p, d, K, T, r, t_i and the prime intervals with η=1/(4d), T/2<S<T are correct. The fixed exponents τ, λ, c, λ', ε, δ are never listed (only κ, in R), nor are α, γ, or the derived α^4θ_i>p.
The map x->∏x_i^{μ_i} as a convolution-preserving isomorphism, implemented by triangular controlled shifts at the paper's cost. μ_i is not defined in the step.
The twist by ζ^k as an isomorphism to C[y]/(y^r+1), with untwisting after ring convolution, matches the paper.
The source transform (A, chirp by ring convolution, B_0, scale 2^γ) and its error 9·2^γ TL·2^{-p} are right. The algorithm list omits Φ^{-1} before the carries (line 4528).

The final error bound 448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding to c_j<2^{3b} and the carries are right. T4.8 says the rescaling is by S and 2^{2b+4}, but the paper uses S and then 2^{2b+4}S. The error chain E_s, E_w is not given.

It states seven normalized terms each at most p^{1-2κ}, smallest margin 2^{-181}=2κ, and the total O(n(lg n)^{1-κ}). The seven terms are not listed, and neither is the fact that g_2=εc(1-τ) is the minimum.
R relies on 'nlogn-conjecture' but no step explains why an O(n(lg n)^{1-κ}) machine refutes the eventual lower bound.

errors.says: The total dimension change s of the labels over all edges is strictly less than Wm (S2 says the same).
errors.paper: The label sum is Wm-2N+2L. The bit network's rank sum s_b is W_b m-N+2L_b, because the N source edges have rank one with no dimension change, so s is not the label dimension change for the bit network.

errors.says: The net operator on each routed role equals D_sink D_source^{-1}.
errors.paper: The route applies ε_w D_sink(ρ(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, with the scalar sign of the signed role permutation.

errors.says: Telescoping gives C^{⊗m} on every role.
errors.paper: Telescoping gives C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates for X_a->Y_a, plus a sign. C^{⊗m} on every role holds only after the Z_a source and sink corrections, the scalar i^27, and negating and un-exchanging the X outputs.

errors.says: With a=s/W<m^λ the recurrence unrolls to O(d^{λ'}).
errors.paper: The leaf contribution uses a<=m^σ to get e^σ d^{β(1-σ)}, which is why λ'>max{λ, σ+β(1-σ)}. With only a<m^λ the leaf exponent would be λ+β(1-λ), which exceeds the chosen λ'.

errors.says: Rescaling by S and 2^{2b+4} undoes the normalizations.
errors.paper: The first scaling is by S and the second by 2^{2b+4}S. The second S reverses the normalization still present in w=(u*v)/S.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: one bank-exchange network gives both tape procedures (S3 interchange, S4 butterfly layer), these feed the synthetic transforms and convolution (T2), resampling and the chirp (T3), and the final assembly and cost count (T4). The address-interchange recursion and the layer recursion are reconstructed well. The plan thins out at the central saving: S2.3 asserts s<Wm without the decreasing central edges, the rank-equals-dimension-change argument, the budget Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, or L/N<1/2. Most of T2 to T4 are quoted statements rather than derivations.

steps.note: The plan has the gadget on three-element subsets of [100], the three stages, (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoration of every scratch wire. The counts N=C(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are not given.

S2.2 has a common invertible frame per gate commuting with pointwise gates, D_vD_u^{-1} on edges and endpoint frames fixing the route operator. S2 says the edges cost only the frame change. The sign ε_w is omitted.

Nondegenerate nested labels from tensored triple lines in an m-dimensional space are named. The defining fact that the only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h, is absent.
S2's motivation says the cost is measured by dimension lost, but there is no P_V-P_U, no rank=dim V-dim U, and no rank-one exception at the N source edges.
A total dimension change is named, but neither Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich nor s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b appears.
s<Wm is asserted, but L/N=100/539 or 101/539 and the positive deficit N-2L are absent.
S2.4 states that endpoint matrices differ by I_m on every input role, giving the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) on every role array. S3.3 extends this to scratch rows.
S3.1 states A=E_1ΠE_2 with a ones and exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and S3.5 has s calls per node. The one-interchange implementation of each elementary shear is not spelled out.

S3.5 and its sub-steps give children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), τ=1-2^{-50} with s/W<m^τ, and F_k=O(e^τ). The justification η>20·2^{-50} with log m<20 appears only as 'the relative rank deficits allow'.

central.summary: The plan has the fixed exchange network, frames, the endpoint shear identity, edges as recursive calls and the recurrence with τ=1-2^{-50}. It asserts rather than reconstructs the core of the saving: which edges decrease, rank equal to dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L and L/N<1/2. So the reason s<Wm is missing.
